title: reserved-seats-and-tables.html
content: Reserved {{variable.Object_Table}} s and {{variable.Object_Seat}} s allows you to create, organize, and track multiple seating plans for any {{variable.Object_Event}} . There are two methods for creating and editing {{variable.Object_Table}} s and {{variable.Object_Seat}} s. Use the Table Manager Manually Create Records Table Manager Known Limitations Attendees who only have the {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_FirstName}} field populated will show as “FirstName undefined” in the Table Manager. Please enter their {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_LastName}} to avoid this issue. Using the Blackthorn | Events (Limited Access) permission set results in an error when removing an Attendee from a Seat because of a missing permission. Manually creating table and seat assignments can be difficult and often results in duplicate {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s. The {{variable.Product_Events}} {{variable.Component_TableManager}} is a new Salesforce Lightning component located on the {{variable.Object_Event}} object designed to efficiently manage your {{variable.Object_Event}} ’s table and seat assignments. It’s as easy as dragging and dropping {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s into {{variable.Object_Table}} and {{variable.Object_Seat}} assignments. This user-friendly tool offers the following functionality. Intuitive Drag-and-Drop Interface: Easily assign {{variable.Object_Table}} s and {{variable.Object_Seat}} s by dragging {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s right where you want them. Efficiency: Reduce the effort required and the potential for errors in table and seat management. The tool can bulk-assign {{variable.Object_Seat}} s and support up to 100 {{variable.Object_Table}} s with 10 {{variable.Object_Seat}} s each. Improved User Experience: Visualize and alter {{variable.Object_Attendee}} seating as needed. Validations: Prevent users from exceeding established limits on assignments and changes between saves. Use Cases Gala Dinners: Ensure VIP guests are seated according to preferences and {{variable.Object_Event}} requirements. Corporate Events: Simplify the process of seating employees and guests at large-scale meetings or parties. Permission Sets The {{variable.PS_ET_Admin}} and {{variable.PS_ET_Organizer}} permission sets have full access to the {{variable.Component_TableManager}} . The {{variable.PS_ET_LimitedAccess}} permission set can use the {{variable.Component_TableManager}} to do everything but delete {{variable.Object_Table}} s. The {{variable.PS_ET_LiteUser}} and {{variable.PS_ET_ReadOnly}} permission sets can only read the information in the {{variable.Component_TableManager}} . Functionality Users can perform the following tasks with the {{variable.Component_TableManager}} . Create new {{variable.Object_Table}} s. Drag and drop {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s on a {{variable.Object_Table}} or {{variable.Object_Seat}} to assign them to that spot. Move {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s between {{variable.Object_Table}} s and {{variable.Object_Seat}} s. Edit existing {{variable.Object_Table}} s and {{variable.Object_Seat}} s. Upload records into {{variable.Object_Table}} s and {{variable.Object_Seat}} s Filter and search for {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s by {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_RegistrStatus}} or name. Use the Assign All button to assign registered {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s to available {{variable.Object_Seat}} s. Any changes saved using the {{variable.Component_TableManager}} will create or update the related {{variable.Object_Table}} and/or {{variable.Object_Seat}} records How It Works Newly created {{variable.Object_Table}} s cannot exceed 10 {{variable.Object_Seat}} s per {{variable.Object_Table}} or 100 {{variable.Object_Table}} s per {{variable.Object_Event}} . If you need more {{variable.Object_Table}} s or {{variable.Object_Seat}} s, you must create them outside of the {{variable.Component_TableManager}} . If you create {{variable.Object_Table}} or {{variable.Object_Seat}} records via a {{variable.SFTerm_RelatedList}} , these validations do not apply. For example, from the {{variable.Object_Event}} ’s {{variable.Object_Table}} s {{variable.SFTerm_RelatedList}} , you can create a {{variable.Object_Table}} with 11 {{variable.Object_Seat}} s or add 101 {{variable.Object_Table}} s to an {{variable.Object_Event}} . But when loading {{variable.Object_Table}} s created outside of the {{variable.Component_TableManager}} , only {{variable.Object_Table}} s that meet the 10 {{variable.Object_Seat}} s per {{variable.Object_Table}} or 100 {{variable.Object_Table}} s per {{variable.Object_Event}} criteria will be loaded in the {{variable.Component_TableManager}} . If you try to view {{variable.Object_Table}} s that exceed those criteria, you will see the following message. “Tables with over 10 seats or exceeding 100 tables will not load. To use the Blackthorn Table Manager, adjust the Tables and Seats configured to align with these requirements.” Table Manager Layout The left “Unassigned” column lists the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s who are registered for the {{variable.Object_Event}} . The right-hand side shows the {{variable.Object_Table}} s and {{variable.Object_Seat}} s. Each {{variable.Object_Table}} has a Pencil (edit) and Trash Can (delete) button located next to the {{variable.Object_Table}} ’s {{variable.Field_Event_Table_TableName}} . Each assigned {{variable.Object_Seat}} at a {{variable.Object_Table}} has a {{variable.Field_Event_Seat_SeatNumber}} next to the assigned {{variable.Object_Attendee}} ’s name. Users can create a new {{variable.Object_Table}} with either a {{variable.Field_Event_Table_TableName}} or a {{variable.Field_Event_Table_TableNumber}} . {{variable.Object_Table}} s with names will be sorted alphabetically. {{variable.Object_Table}} s with numbers will be sorted by number, lowest to highest. If a {{variable.Object_Table}} has both a {{variable.Field_Event_Table_TableName}} and a {{variable.Field_Event_Table_TableNumber}} , the {{variable.Field_Event_Table_TableName}} will be displayed and sorted alphabetically. Limitations Newly created {{variable.Object_Table}} s in the {{variable.Component_TableManager}} cannot exceed 10 {{variable.Object_Seat}} s per {{variable.Object_Table}} or 100 {{variable.Object_Table}} s per {{variable.Object_Event}} . You must click {{variable.Button_Save}} before closing the browser window; otherwise, you will lose your changes. Dropping a second {{variable.Object_Attendee}} on top of an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} ’s name replaces the original {{variable.Object_Attendee}} . It does not “shuffle” the other {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s at the {{variable.Object_Table}} , as many drag-and-drop interfaces do. Long {{variable.Object_Attendee}} names may not be fully displayed. (maximum character restriction) Set Up the Table Manager Before you can use the {{variable.Component_TableManager}} , you must add it to the {{variable.Object_Event}} record. Note: You must be a Salesforce Admin to perform the following steps. Open an {{variable.Object_Event}} record. (It can be any {{variable.Object_Event}} record.) Click the {{variable.Button_GearIcon}} . Click Edit Page . (This will launch the Lightning App Builder.) Click in the navigation tab above the {{variable.Object_Event}} information. Click Add Tab . The newly added tab will automatically be labeled as “Details.” Click Details (the new tab). Set {{variable.Field_SF_TabLabel}} = “Custom” Set {{variable.Field_SF_CustomLabel}} = “Table Manager” Click {{variable.Button_Done}} . Click More in the navigation tab. Click Table Manager . In the Custom–Managed section of the Components menu, find “BT Events Table Manager.” Drag and drop the component onto the page. Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Click Activation: Event Record Page . Review the settings and click Close . Click the Back Arrow . Click More . Click Table Manager . You now have access to the Table Manager tool! How to Use the Table Manager Create a Table Click Add New Table to add a new {{variable.Object_Table}} to the {{variable.Object_Event}} . Fill in the following fields. {{variable.Field_Event_Table_TableName}} and/or a {{variable.Field_Event_Table_TableNumber}} (If a {{variable.Object_Table}} has both a {{variable.Field_Event_Table_TableName}} and a {{variable.Field_Event_Table_TableNumber}} , the {{variable.Field_Event_Table_TableName}} will be displayed and sorted alphabetically.) {{variable.Field_Event_Table_TotalSeats}} (required) Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Add Attendees to a Table There are multiple ways to search for and add {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s to a {{variable.Object_Table}} . {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s who have not been assigned to a {{variable.Object_Table}} will be in the column labeled Unassigned. Drag and drop each {{variable.Object_Attendee}} ’s name to a {{variable.Object_Seat}} at the {{variable.Object_Table}} . If there are more than 100 {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s in the list, you must use the search feature since loading the full list could impact performance. Click Assign All to assign all {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s to the {{variable.Object_Table}} s. Use the Search Attendee Name search box to locate an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} . Use the Filter By search feature to filter {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s by name or {{variable.Field_Attendee_RegistratStatus}} . Click Save Changes to save any changes before closing the browser window; otherwise, you will lose your changes. Edit a Table Click the {{variable.Button_Pencil}} icon on the {{variable.Object_Table}} you want to edit. Update the information. Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Delete a Table {{variable.Object_Table}} s with assigned {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s cannot be deleted until all {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s are deleted from the {{variable.Object_Table}} . Remove {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s from the {{variable.Object_Table}} . Drag and drop an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} ’s name from the {{variable.Object_Table}} to the Unassigned column. Repeat the process until the {{variable.Object_Table}} is empty. Click Save Changes . Click the Trash Can icon on the {{variable.Object_Table}} you want to delete. Click Yes . Manually Create and Edit Records Create a Table Record Open and existing {{variable.Object_Event}} record. Go to the {{variable.Object_Table}} s {{variable.SFTerm_RelatedList}} and click {{variable.button_new}} .   Fill in the following fields {{variable.Field_Event_Table_TableName}} {{variable.Field_Event_Table_TableNumber}} {{variable.Field_Event_Table_TotalSeats}} (required) {{variable.Field_Table_Account}} {{variable.Field_Table_MainContactAttende}} {{variable.Field_Table_MainContactContact}}   Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . The {{variable.Field_Event_Table_SeatsAvailab}} and {{variable.Field_Event_Table_SeatAssigned}} fields will automatically update. Assign Seats There are two ways to assign {{variable.Object_Seat}} s to {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s. The first is to create a {{variable.Object_Seat}} record and assign the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} to the {{variable.Object_Seat}} record. The second is to go to the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} record and assign them from there. Create a Seat Record Go to the {{variable.Object_Table}} record. Click {{variable.button_new}} next to the {{variable.Object_Seat}} s {{variable.SFTerm_RelatedList}} . Fill in the following fields. {{variable.Field_Event_Seat_SeatNumber}} {{variable.Field_Seat_Attendee}} If the {{variable.Object_Seat}} is related to a {{variable.Object_Table}} at a {{variable.Object_Session}} , fill in the {{variable.Field_Seat_Session}} and {{variable.Field_Seat_SessionAttendee}} fields as well.   Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Here’s the new {{variable.Object_Seat}} record. You will also see the new {{variable.Object_Seat}} record in the {{variable.Object_Table}} ’s {{variable.Object_Seat}} s {{variable.SFTerm_RelatedList}} . The {{variable.Object_Event}} and related {{variable.Object_Contact}} records will update automatically. Assign an Attendee to a Seat Record Once an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} has registered for your {{variable.Object_Event}} , you can create a {{variable.Object_Seat}} record for them. Open the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} record. Click {{variable.button_new}} next to the {{variable.Object_Seat}} s {{variable.SFTerm_RelatedList}} . Fill in the following fields. {{variable.Field_Event_Seat_Table}} {{variable.Field_Event_Seat_SeatNumber}} If the {{variable.Object_Seat}} is related to a {{variable.Object_Table}} at a {{variable.Object_Session}} , fill in the {{variable.Field_Seat_Session}} and {{variable.Field_Seat_SessionAttendee}} fields as well.   Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Here’s the new {{variable.Object_Seat}} record. You will also see the new {{variable.Object_Seat}} record in the {{variable.Object_Table}} ’s {{variable.Object_Seat}} s {{variable.SFTerm_RelatedList}} . The {{variable.Object_Event}} and related {{variable.Object_Contact}} records will update automatically.
